result:
Not quite the right move, Riley — the question bakes in a premise that doesn't hold for what you're building.

PPO (the RL algorithm behind a lot of model training) is how a *lab* polishes a model before it's ever released — it's baked into the weights before you ever touch the thing. You're not training a model at all for the makerspace assistant; you're calling an already-trained model through an API and shaping how well it uses tools through good tool descriptions, clear prompts, and smart loop design. That's also explicitly off the table for your mission — the math inside training is out of scope, and honestly, out of reach on three hours a week with a small budget anyway. PPO training needs huge compute, a reward signal, and infrastructure way past "senior design project."

Think of it like your IT job: you don't rebuild the database engine to get good query results — you write good queries and design good indexes. Same here: you don't retrain the model to get good tool calls — you write a tight, unambiguous tool description ("books equipment time; needs equipment_id, start time, end time; returns confirmation or a conflict error") and the existing model does the rest. That's the lever you actually have.

When *would* RL training matter? If you were the lab building the base model, or you had massive scale and a very specific behavior no amount of prompting could fix. Not your situation.

Does that distinction click — what the model's maker did once with RL, versus what you do every day by writing a good tool description?
